passages.text: Hunt and Lipo contend that moai-building was an activity that helped keep the peace between islanders. They also believe that moving the moai required few people and no wood, because they were walked upright. On that issue, Hunt and Lipo say, archaeological evidence backs up Rapanui folklore. Recent experiments indicate that as few as 18 people could, with three strong ropes and a bit of practice, easily manoeuvre a 1,000 kg moai replica a few hundred metres. The figures’ fat bellies tilted them forward, and a D-shaped base allowed handlers to roll and rock them side to side.
passages.translation: 亨特和利波认为，建造摩艾石像有助于维持岛民之间的和平。他们还相信，搬运石像只需少量人力，无需木材，因为石像是直立着“走”过去的。他们说，考古证据支持拉帕努伊人的民间传说。近期实验表明，只要三根结实的绳索和少量练习，最少18个人就能轻松地将一座重1,000公斤的石像复制品移动数百米。石像鼓起的腹部使它向前倾，而D形底座使搬运者能将它左右滚动、摇摆。

passages.text: Pharmaceutical science and chemistry built on these ancient foundations and perfected the extraction, characterisation, modification and testing of these natural products. Then, for a while, modern pharmaceutical science moved its focus away from nature and into the laboratory, designing chemical compounds from scratch. The main cause of this shift is that although there are plenty of promising chemical compounds in nature, finding them is far from easy. Securing sufficient numbers of the organism in question, isolating and characterising the compounds of interest, and producing large quantities of these compounds are all significant hurdles.
passages.translation: 制药科学和化学以这些古老的基础为起点，完善了对天然产物的提取、特性分析、改造和测试。后来有一段时间，现代制药科学将注意力从自然界转向实验室，从零开始设计化合物。这一转变的主要原因是：尽管自然界有大量前景可观的化合物，找到它们却绝非易事。获取足够数量的相关生物，分离和分析感兴趣的化合物，以及大量生产这些化合物，都是重大障碍。

passages.text: If you think about collecting postage stamps, another potential reason for it — or, perhaps, a result of collecting — is its educational value. Stamp collecting opens a window to other countries, and to the plants, animals, or famous people shown on their stamps. Similarly, in the 19th century, many collectors amassed fossils, animals and plants from around the globe, and their collections provided a vast amount of information about the natural world. Without those collections, our understanding would be greatly inferior to what it is.
passages.translation: 以集邮为例，另一个可能的动机——或者说集邮带来的结果——是它的教育价值。集邮为人们了解其他国家，以及邮票上的植物、动物和名人打开了一扇窗。类似地，19世纪的许多收藏家从世界各地收集化石、动植物，他们的收藏为人类提供了大量关于自然界的信息。没有这些收藏，我们的认识就会远不如今天。

passages.text: Pheidole dentata, a native ant of the south-eastern U.S., isn’t immortal. But scientists have found that it doesn’t seem to show any signs of aging. Old worker ants can do everything just as well as the youngsters, and their brains appear just as sharp. ‘We get a picture that these ants really don’t decline,’ says Ysabel Giraldo, who studied the ants for her doctoral thesis at Boston University.
passages.translation: 美国东南部的本土蚂蚁Pheidole dentata并非长生不老，但科学家发现，它们似乎没有表现出任何衰老迹象。老工蚁做任何事情都与年轻工蚁一样出色，头脑也似乎同样敏锐。在波士顿大学攻读博士期间研究这些蚂蚁的伊莎贝尔·吉拉尔多说：“我们观察到的情况是，这些蚂蚁确实没有衰退。”

passages.text: But migration is a complex issue, and biologists define it differently, depending in part on what sorts of animals they study. Joel Berger, of the University of Montana, who works on the American pronghorn and other large terrestrial mammals, prefers what he calls a simple, practical definition suited to his beasts: ‘movements from a seasonal home area away to another home area and back again’. Generally the reason for such seasonal back-and-forth movement is to seek resources that aren't available within a single area year-round.
passages.translation: 不过，迁徙是一个复杂的问题，生物学家对它的定义各不相同，部分原因在于他们研究的动物种类不同。蒙大拿大学的乔尔·伯格研究美洲叉角羚及其他大型陆生哺乳动物，他偏好一个适合这些动物的简单、实用定义：“从一个季节性栖息地迁往另一个栖息地，再返回。”这种季节性的往返通常是为了寻找单一区域无法全年提供的资源。

passages.text: major drawback of vertical farming, however, is that the plants would require artificial light. Without it, those plants nearest the windows would be exposed to more sunlight and grow more quickly, reducing the efficiency of the system. Single-storey greenhouses have the benefit of natural overhead light: even so, many still need artificial lighting. A multi-storey facility with no natural overhead light would require far more. Generating enough light could be prohibitively expensive, unless cheap, renewable energy is available, and this appears to be rather a future aspiration than a likelihood for the near future.
passages.translation: 然而，垂直农业的一大缺点是植物需要人工照明。如果没有人工照明，最靠近窗户的植物会接收到更多阳光，长得更快，从而降低整个系统的效率。单层温室具有天然顶部采光的优势；即便如此，许多温室仍需要人工照明。没有天然顶部采光的多层设施需要的照明会更多。除非有廉价的可再生能源，否则提供足够光照的费用可能高得难以承受，而这看起来更像长远愿景，不像近期能够实现的事情。

passages.text: According to the latest figures, the majority of the world's population is now bilingual or multilingual, having grown up speaking two or more languages. In the past, such children were considered to be at a disadvantage compared with their monolingual peers. Over the past few decades, however, technological advances have allowed researchers to look more deeply at how bilingualism interacts with and changes the cognitive and neurological systems, thereby identifying several clear benefits of being bilingual.
passages.translation: 根据最新数据，如今世界上大多数人会两种或多种语言，从小就使用两种或更多语言。过去，人们认为这些儿童比只会一种语言的同龄人处于劣势。然而，过去几十年的技术进步使研究人员能够更深入地观察双语能力如何与认知和神经系统相互作用并改变它们，从而发现了掌握两种语言的若干明显好处。

passages.text: Two things distinguish food production from all other productive activities: first, every single person needs food each day and has a right to it; and second, it is hugely dependent on nature. These two unique aspects, one political, the other natural, make food production highly vulnerable and different from any other business. At the same time, cultural values are highly entrenched in food and agricultural systems worldwide.
passages.translation: 食品生产有两点不同于其他所有生产活动：第一，每个人每天都需要食物，也都有获得食物的权利；第二，食品生产高度依赖自然。这两种独特属性，一种属于政治层面，另一种属于自然层面，使食品生产非常脆弱，也使它不同于其他行业。与此同时，文化价值观在世界各地的食品与农业体系中都根深蒂固。

passages.text: Researchers study the interactions between humans and their environment that could lead to illness (such as asthma in places with high levels of pollution) and work to create a clear way of categorising illnesses, diseases and epidemics into local and global scales. Health geographers can map the spread of illnesses and attempt to identify the reasons behind an increase or decrease in illnesses, as they work to find a way to halt the further spread or re-emergence of diseases in vulnerable populations.
passages.translation: 研究人员考察人类与环境之间可能导致疾病的相互作用，例如高污染地区的哮喘，并尝试建立清晰的方法，在地方和全球尺度上对疾病与流行病进行分类。健康地理学家可以绘制疾病传播图，尝试找出疾病增多或减少的原因，同时寻找方法，阻止疾病在易受影响的人群中继续传播或再次出现。

passages.text: Archaeologists Terry Hunt of the University of Hawaii and Carl Lipo of California State University agree that Easter Island lost its lush forests and that it was an ‘ecological catastrophe’ — but they believe the islanders themselves weren't to blame. And the moai certainly weren't. Archaeological excavations indicate that the Rapanui went to heroic efforts to protect the resources of their wind-lashed, infertile fields. They built thousands of circular stone windbreaks and gardened inside them, and used broken volcanic rocks to keep the soil moist. In short, Hunt and Lipo argue, the prehistoric Rapanui were pioneers of sustainable farming.
passages.translation: 夏威夷大学的考古学家特里·亨特和加利福尼亚州立大学的卡尔·利波同意，复活节岛失去了茂密的森林，这是一场“生态灾难”，但他们认为责任不在岛民，更不在摩艾石像。考古发掘表明，拉帕努伊人为保护饱受强风侵袭、贫瘠的农田资源付出了巨大努力。他们建造了数千个圆形石制防风围墙，在其中耕作，并用碎火山岩保持土壤湿润。亨特和利波认为，史前拉帕努伊人是可持续农业的先驱。

passages.text: Some plants mainly use day length as an indicator of the season. Other species, such as daffodils, have considerable temperature sensitivity, and can flower months in advance during a warm winter. In fact, the discovery of the dual role of phytochromes provides the science behind a well-known rhyme long used to predict the coming season: oak before ash we’ll have a splash, ash before oak we’re in for a soak.
passages.translation: 有些植物主要通过白昼长度判断季节。其他物种，如水仙，对温度相当敏感，在温暖的冬天可能提前数月开花。事实上，对光敏色素双重作用的发现，为一首长期用来预测季节的熟知歌谣提供了科学依据：橡树先于梣树发叶，雨水就少；梣树先于橡树发叶，就会下个透。

passages.text: There has been a considerable amount of research on high performance over the last century that suggests it goes way beyond tested intelligence. passages.text: La Gomera is one of the Canary Islands situated in the Atlantic Ocean off the northwest coast of Africa. This small volcanic island is mountainous, with steep rocky slopes and deep, wooded ravines, rising to 1,487 metres at its highest peak.
